key_insight: Represent characters as reusable, character-centric "content anchors" extracted from reference views so a generator can reliably preserve identity and multi-view appearance over long video sequences. This outside-looking-in anchoring provides stable memory that improves consistency without relying on non-character context.
problem_solved: Maintains long-duration, multi-view identity and appearance consistency for generated character videos, avoiding drift and identity mismatch that arise when memory is weak or not character-centric.
method: Construct character-centric content anchors from reference frames (multi-view / multi-pose snippets) to serve as a compact, persistent memory representation.
Anchor-conditioned generation: retrieve and fuse anchor features into the video synthesis pipeline so each output frame is grounded to stable identity information.
Train with objectives for identity preservation, multi-view coherence, and temporal consistency to ensure expressive yet consistent long-form character videos.
impact: Enables more reliable, long-form character video synthesis for applications like virtual production, avatars, and animation pipelines by providing a practical memory mechanism for identity preservation. Practitioners can leverage anchor-based memory to reduce identity drift and improve multi-view realism.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: reference frames → content anchor extractor → memory bank → anchor-conditioned generator → output video
Before/after comparison: baseline (identity drift) vs Gloria (consistent multi-view appearance) across a long timeline
Anchor visualization: overlay of extracted anchor features mapped to reference frames to show what information is preserved
Metrics chart: identity-consistency and temporal-coherence scores vs sequence length for baseline and Gloria
paper_title: Gloria: Consistent Character Video Generation via Content Anchors
paper_authors: Yuhang Yang, Fan Zhang, Huaijin Pi, Shuai Guo, Guowei Xu
